mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPI YoY growth exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where UNRATE drops by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in a month signals increased demand for housing and related goods, boosting economic activity and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where HOUST increases by more than 10% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month indicates a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face reduced output and profitability.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO drops by more than 2% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is above 2% YoY, it signals a supportive monetary policy in a growing economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 1% and GDPC1 YoY growth exceeds 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where PAYEMS increases for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 5% YoY and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5%, it signals strong consumer demand and a healthy labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS YoY growth exceeds 5% and UNRATE is below 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% in a month.
